doc_name: American Classical Music Hall of Fame and Museum
text: The American Classical Music Hall of Fame and Museum is a non-profit organization dedicated to honoring individuals and institutions that have made significant contributions to classical music—specifically, "people who have contributed to American music and music in America," as stated by Samuel Adler, co-chairman of the organization's first artistic directorate. The organization was established in 1996 by Cincinnati businessman and civic leader David A. Klingshirm and began inducting honorees in 1998. Its offices and exhibits are located in the Hamilton County Memorial Building, adjacent to the Cincinnati Music Hall in the Over-the-Rhine neighborhood of Cincinnati, Ohio. While the exhibits are not open to the public, they are accessible during certain events at the School for Creative and Performing Arts in Cincinnati and through a virtual museum. In 2012, the "Classical Walk of Fame" was inaugurated in Washington Park, outside the steps of the Cincinnati Music Hall, featuring pavement stones inscribed with the names of American Classical Music Hall of Fame inductees. A mobile app enables park visitors to read biographies of the inductees, listen to samples of their music, view related images, and play classical music through a mobile jukebox that activates the park's "dancing fountain."
